title: Highest mode — divinity in Christ hypostatically, bodily
source_text: XXVIII. Praecipue vero longe perfectissimo & ineffabili modo Deus est in Christo homine, in quo tam excellenter habitat divinitas, ut ipse vere & proprie Deus esse dicatur. Unde dictum est a Paulo omnem plenitudinem divinitatis in eo habitare somatikos, corporaliter. Corporaliter, inquam, non tantum, ut id opponatur figurae, secundum quam Deus in templo Judaico, & in arca foederis esse & habitare dicebatur: sed maxime propter hypostaticam illam unionem, qua divina natura cum humana & concreta in unam convenit personam; ut vere dicere liceat divinitatem incarnatam, atque ut ita loquar, incorporatam esse.
pass_a_gloss: But especially in a far most perfect and ineffable mode God is in the man Christ, in whom deity dwells so excellently that He Himself is said truly and properly to be God. Whence it was said by Paul that all the fullness of deity dwells in Him somatikos, bodily. Bodily, I say, not only as opposed to the figure according to which God was said to be and dwell in the Jewish temple and in the ark of the covenant: but chiefly because of that hypostatic union by which the divine nature comes together with the human and concrete into one person; so that it is truly permitted to say that deity is incarnate, and so to speak, incorporate.
pass_b_english: Highest mode: deity in the man Christ — He is truly God.
Col 2 somatikos / bodily: beyond temple-figure presence.
Hypostatic union: divinity incarnate / incorporate in one person.
